data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding decreased from GBP 59.471m at the opening of the year to GBP 35.077m at 31 December 2023. Prior-year development from underwriting years at or before 2021 produced a small gross release (approximately GBP 1.735m), driven by favourable claims development and payments, partly influenced by commutation/Reinsurance-to-Close activity and foreign exchange movements. The syndicate writes US property catastrophe reinsurance and the reserve movements relate predominantly to Property catastrophe lines.
raw_causal_phrases: The movement in the net provisions for claims includes an improvement of GBP 3.4m in respect of reserves set in prior years (2022: deterioration of GBP 3.4m).
In 2023, there has been an overall surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 2.9m (2022: deficit of GBP 1.7m).
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision' line was presented. Prior-year development (gross) was calculated from the published gross claims development triangle (page 25) giving an approximate gross release of GBP 1.735m. The notes also state a net improvement of GBP 3.4m (net of reinsurance) which differs from the gross triangle-based calculation. RITC commutations and foreign exchange movements materially affect comparisons and may distort the triangle; amounts in the report are presented in GBP '000 and have been converted to millions for this output.
